## 5. Removed Test-Only Dependencies

**None.**

### Python (`backend/requirements.txt`)

No test-only packages were present. `pytest`, `pytest-django`, `coverage`, `factory_boy`, `mock`, `faker`, and `hypothesis` are all absent from `requirements.txt`. The CI pipeline uses Django's built-in `manage.py test` framework (bundled with Django itself). pytest was used only via a manually installed local virtualenv, with no declared dependency.

### JavaScript (`frontend/package.json`)

No test-only packages were present. The `devDependencies` contain only ESLint, TypeScript, Vite, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, PostCSS, Autoprefixer, Tailwind CSS, and `@types/*` packages — all build and type tooling. No jest, vitest, Playwright, Cypress, `@testing-library`, or any other JavaScript testing framework was found.

## 9. Remaining Test-Related Files That Could Not Be Safely Removed

**None.** All identified test-only files were confirmed safe to delete and have been removed.

The three documentation files that describe testing procedures — `docs/load_testing.md`, `docs/recovery_testing.md`, and `docs/user_acceptance_testing.md` — were deliberately preserved. They are not test infrastructure; they describe production backup health verification, human release sign-off procedures, and endpoint performance thresholds. Removing them would destroy operational knowledge without yielding any production code benefit.
